answer: Make every agent lock a deposit in a harbor escrow contract before it can trade: the escrow holds the deposit while peers verify the agent's work, releasing it only after a clean history accrues. Each agent signs its work with a rotating cipher key tied to one long-lived identity, so a sybil attacker must fund and age each fake separately. A sable audit list flags keys whose deposit-to-work ratio looks anomalous, making mass fakery expensive while honest agents get their deposit back.
